claims.claim: Tailwind CSS v4 is current; v4.3.0 was released on May 8, 2026 (latest patch 4.3.3). v4 is configured in CSS via @import "tailwindcss" and runs through a build plugin (@tailwindcss/vite, @tailwindcss/postcss or @tailwindcss/webpack).
claims.raw_snippet: May 8, 2026 Tailwind CSS v4.3: Scrollbars, new colors, and more

claims.claim: The logical inset utilities start-*/end-* were deprecated in favor of inset-s-*/inset-e-* in Tailwind CSS v4.2.0, released 18 February 2026, aligning them with inset-bs-*/inset-be-* (old names still work); margin/padding ms-/me-/ps-/pe- are unaffected.
claims.raw_snippet: Deprecate `start-*` and `end-*` utilities in favor of `inset-s-*` and `inset-e-*` utilities
claims.source_note: The entry sits under '## [4.2.0] - 2026-02-18' (see tailwind-v42-release-date). The v4.3 blog post recaps the rename but carries neither the version number of the change nor its date. The 'margin/padding unaffected' half is verified by compiling ms-4, me-4, ps-4 and pe-4 against tailwindcss 4.3.3.

claims.claim: Tailwind v4's rtl: and ltr: variants compile to :where(:dir(rtl), [dir="rtl"], [dir="rtl"] *) and the ltr mirror. So ltr: applies on a page with no dir, and a nested dir="auto" island resolving to LTR inside an RTL page matches both variants.
claims.raw_snippet: rtl & :where(:dir(rtl), [dir="rtl"], [dir="rtl"] *) ltr & :where(:dir(ltr), [dir="ltr"], [dir="ltr"] *)
claims.verification_note:
Chromium test 2026-09-26 on tailwindcss 4.3.3 output: in , a

containing English gets both rtl:text-red-500 and ltr:underline; with no dir anywhere, ltr:underline applies.

claims.claim: A Tailwind theme variable that references another variable (e.g. --font-sans: var(--font-heebo) from next/font) should use @theme inline: without it the utility references the theme variable, which CSS resolves where it is defined, so utilities can resolve to unexpected values.
claims.raw_snippet: your utility classes might resolve to unexpected values because of how variables are resolved in CSS
claims.verification_note: Chromium test 2026-09-26 with tailwindcss 4.3.3 output: next/font-style variable on <html>: both @theme and @theme inline resolve; variable on <body>: .font-sans resolves only with inline, and the Preflight default font on html falls back to the Tailwind sans stack in BOTH cases. The build succeeds in all cases.

claims.claim: In Tailwind v4 the darkMode config key is gone; class-based dark mode is opted into in CSS with @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *));.
claims.raw_snippet: Toggling dark mode manually If you want your dark theme to be driven by a CSS selector instead of the prefers-color-scheme media query, override the dark variant to use your custom selector: app.css @import "tailwindcss" ; @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .

claims.claim: font-display: swap gives the font face an extremely small block period and an infinite swap period, so fallback text shows almost at once and the web font swaps in when loaded (mitigating FOIT).

claims.claim: In Tailwind v4 each @theme variable namespace generates the matching utilities, so leading-hebrew / leading-hebrew-tight / leading-hebrew-relaxed exist only if --leading-hebrew*, not --leading-tight/normal/relaxed, are defined.
claims.raw_snippet: Theme variables are defined in namespaces and each namespace corresponds to one or more utility class or variant APIs.
claims.verified_via: compiled against tailwindcss 4.3.3 with @tailwindcss/cli: the old @theme block emitted only .font-hebrew; the corrected block emitted .leading-hebrew, .leading-hebrew-tight and .leading-hebrew-relaxed
claims.source_note: The namespace table on the same page carries the row "--leading-* Line height utilities like leading-tight", and the sentence "Defining new theme variables in these namespaces will make new corresponding utilities and variants available in your project:" introduces it. Quoted here as one contiguous sentence; the table row is a separate HTML table cell and cannot be spliced into the same quote.

claims.claim: In Tailwind v4 space-x-* compiles to margin-inline-start / margin-inline-end and is therefore direction-aware; space-x-reverse is for reversed DOM order (flex-row-reverse), not for RTL, and rtl:space-x-reverse puts the spacing on the wrong side. gap-* remains preferred for flex and grid.
claims.raw_snippet: use the space-x-reverse or space-y-reverse utilities to ensure the space is added to the correct side of each element
claims.verified_via: compiled against tailwindcss 4.3.3: :where(.space-x-4 > :not(:last-child)) { --tw-space-x-reverse: 0; margin-inline-start: calc(calc(var(--spacing) * 4) * var(--tw-space-x-reverse)); margin-inline-end: calc(calc(var(--spacing) * 4) * calc(1 - var(--tw-space-x-reverse))); } and .rtl\:space-x-reverse sets --tw-space-x-reverse: 1

claims.claim: The v4 documented spelling for linear gradients is bg-linear-to-r / bg-linear-to-l; bg-gradient-to-* still compiles as a legacy alias.
Tailwind ships block-axis logical spacing utilities mbs-*/mbe-*, pbs-*/pbe-* and border-bs/border-be-*, available in v4.3 (added in v4.2 and documented in the v4.3 release post).
claims.raw_snippet: For spacing, there are new block-start and block-end utilities for padding, margin, scroll padding, scroll margin, and borders:

The class names sit in a separate code block, so they are not quoted inside the sentence.
claims.verified_via: mbs-4, mbe-4, pbs-4, pbe-4, border-bs and border-be-2 all compile in tailwindcss 4.3.3

claims.claim: Tailwind ships logical sizing utilities inline-*/block-* with min and max variants (min-inline-*, max-block-*), available in v4.3 (added in v4.2 and documented in the v4.3 release post).
claims.raw_snippet: We've also added logical sizing utilities for inline-size and block-size , along with min and max variants:
claims.source_note: The code sample directly under this sentence shows block-64 inline-full max-block-screen max-inline-lg min-block-24 min-inline-0. Spacing inside the quote follows the rendered page, which separates the inline code spans with whitespace.
claims.verified_via: inline-40, block-20, min-inline-0 and max-block-full all compile in tailwindcss 4.3.3

claims.claim: Tailwind v4 auto-detects template sources; paths it does not scan (for example a dependency listed in .gitignore) are registered in CSS with the @source directive, relative to the stylesheet.
claims.raw_snippet: Use @source to explicitly register source paths relative to the stylesheet
claims.verified_via: source fetched 2026-09-20 and the passage copied verbatim from the cited page

claims.claim: Tailwind recommends gap utilities over space-x/space-y for wrapped or complex layouts.
claims.raw_snippet: For those situations, it's better to use the gap utilities when possible

claims.claim: Dependencies are usually listed in .gitignore and ignored by Tailwind's automatic source detection, so an external component library must be registered with @source.
claims.raw_snippet: since dependencies are usually listed in your .gitignore file and ignored by Tailwind by default

claims.claim: Tailwind CSS v4.2.0 added the @tailwindcss/webpack package, a webpack loader listed after css-loader in the .css rule.
claims.raw_snippet: Add @tailwindcss/webpack package to run Tailwind CSS as a webpack plugin
claims.verification_note: Package README (tailwindlabs/tailwindcss packages/@tailwindcss-webpack) describes it as 'A webpack loader for Tailwind CSS v4' with use: [MiniCssExtractPlugin.loader, 'css-loader', '@tailwindcss/webpack']; npm @tailwindcss/webpack 4.3.3.

claims.claim: Tailwind v4 Preflight takes the page's default font family from the --font-sans theme variable, and form controls inherit it (font: inherit), so pointing --font-sans at a Hebrew stack makes Hebrew the default.
claims.raw_snippet: --default-font-family: --theme(--font-sans, initial);
claims.verification_note: tailwindcss 4.3.3 preflight.css applies font-family: --theme(--default-font-family, ...) on html and 'font: inherit' on button/input/select/optgroup/textarea.

claims.claim: A flex row's main axis follows the text direction, so under dir=rtl the first item is placed at the right; adding row-reverse puts it at the inline-end (left), restoring LTR visual order.
claims.raw_snippet: the flex container's main-axis is defined to be the same as the text direction
claims.verification_note: tailwindcss 4.3.3 compiles rtl:flex-row-reverse to a plain flex-direction: row-reverse under :where(:dir(rtl), [dir="rtl"], [dir="rtl"] *).
